vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 2.3.4

The skill bundle is a legitimate customer service template generator. The primary script, `scripts/cs.sh`, is a Python-based tool that generates text responses for various e-commerce scenarios (presale, complaints, refunds) based on user input. A secondary utility script, `scripts/script.sh`, provides basic local data logging and management features but contains no network activity, credential access, or malicious logic.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions align with its customer-service reply purpose and do not request external credentials or network access, though it creates local data/log files and the shipped SKILL.md contains unicode control characters (possible obfuscation) worth inspecting before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the provided artifacts: an executable shell wrapper (cs.sh) that runs an embedded Python generator, a utility script that manages a small local data directory, and a tips.md with guidance. There are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or external services required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running scripts locally (bash scripts/cs.sh). The runtime instructions stay within the stated purpose (generate reply templates and FAQs). Note: the included utility script creates and writes to a local data directory under $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME/.local/share/customer-service-reply — the skill persists logs and a data.log locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no network downloads. This is instruction-only with bundled scripts, so nothing is fetched from remote hosts during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The only env-like behavior is that scripts honor an optional CUSTOMER_SERVICE_REPLY_DIR to change their local data directory; that's proportional and documented in the script.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated privileges, but it does persist user data and logs under the user's home directory (default: ~/.local/share/customer-service-reply). This is reasonable for a local utility but users should be aware of the local write footprint.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its described purpose: it runs a local Python-based generator (via cs.sh) and a small utility that stores logs/data in a $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME location. Before installing or running: 1) Inspect the full SKILL.md and the two scripts for any unexpected commands (look for network calls like curl/wget, or eval/exec of downloaded code). 2) Remove or investigate any strange/unexpected unicode control characters in SKILL.md (they may hide text). 3) If you want to limit persistence, set CUSTOMER_SERVICE_REPLY_DIR to a dedicated sandbox directory or run the scripts inside a container. 4) Because the provided cs.sh output in the manifest is truncated, if possible verify the complete script contents locally; if you cannot, run it in an isolated environment first. Overall the package looks benign and local-only, but take the above precautions before granting access to your main environment.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The SKILL.md contains unicode control characters flagged by the pre-scan. This is not required for a customer-service template generator and may be used to hide or obfuscate content; review the SKILL.md for invisible characters before trusting the package.
